title: Building Multimodal AI Agents From Scratch — Apoorva Joshi, MongoDB
talk_summary: A MongoDB developer advocate workshop that explains agent components (perception, planning, tools, memory) and builds a from-scratch multimodal RAG agent over text+image documents. The one substantive technique is screenshotting document pages and embedding them with a VLM-based multimodal embedding model to avoid CLIP's modality gap and complex extraction pipelines.

takeaways.technique: Page-screenshot multimodal retrieval instead of extract-chunk-summarize
takeaways.what_they_do: Render each document page to an image, embed the whole page with a VLM-based multimodal embedding model, store only the image reference plus embedding in the vector DB, and fetch the image from blob storage at retrieval time so text and figures stay together as context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you simply take a screenshot of it pass it through a multimodal embedding model and the embedding that you get from that makes this data ready for retrieval

takeaways.technique: Avoid CLIP modality gap with unified-encoder embeddings
takeaways.what_they_do: Chooses VLM-architecture embedding models where text and images share one encoder, because CLIP-style dual encoders put irrelevant same-modality items closer than relevant cross-modality items.
takeaways.evidence_quote: irrelevant items of the same modality end up uh close to each other rather than uh relevant items of different modalities

takeaways.what_they_do: Retrieves whole pages rather than small chunks to preserve text-figure continuity, and suggests adding overlap or fetching previous/next pages to recover boundary context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whenever you're retrieving a page you could do something like retrieve the previous two next two pages

takeaways.technique: Session-ID keyed short-term memory in a DB
takeaways.what_they_do: Each query carries a session ID; the agent loads prior turns for that session, passes them as context on every LLM call, and appends the new query+response back; tool calls and reasoning traces optionally logged.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each user query is associated with a session ID just as some identifier to distinguish between different conversations

takeaways.technique: Use agents only for unpredictable, latency-tolerant tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly recommends simple prompting or RAG for structured tasks and reserves agents for multi-step, non-deterministic, high-latency-tolerance work, warning agents carry higher cost and latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: only use agents if you need to. Don't complicate whatever it is you're trying to build
